title: Smith, Lee, Trenaman help Hurricanes break duck
excerpt: Meanwhile, Sydney Sixers sealed their playoff berth with a win over Perth Scorchers
author: Cricbuzz Staff
body: Eight games in, the Hobart Hurricanes finally got on the board, registering their first win of the season by beating the Sydney Thunder in Hobart. A three-wicket haul from Linsey Smith followed by an unbeaten 55 from Rachel Trenaman saw the Hurricanes register a comfortable eight-wicket win.

Opting to bowl first, the Hurricanes managed to keep Georgia Voll quiet and had her dismissed off the last ball of the Powerplay. Phoebe Litchfield provided early impetus but was out offering a return catch to Linsey Smith in the sixth over.

Anika Learoyd and Heather Knight got off to starts but were both dismissed for 18 by Lauren Smith and Linsey Smith respectively. It was a 56-run stand between Nadine de Klerk (36*) and Tahlia Wilson (29) that really moved the needle for the Thunder. Linsey Smith returned to break the partnership in the 19th over by dismissing Wilson as the Thunder finished with 150 for 5.

In reply, the Hurricanes’ openers got the team off to a brisk start, making 40 for 0 by the end of the Powerplay. Lizelle Lee struck three fours and four sixes in her 22-ball 42 before falling to Samantha Bates in the sixth over. Kate Pelle then fell to Jemma Barsby for a run-a-ball 18 in the eighth.

An unbeaten 80-run partnership followed as Trenaman and Nicola Carey batted with freedom. Eight boundaries were struck in the space of 13 deliveries starting with the first ball of the 14th over as the Hurricanes got over the line with nearly five overs to spare.
The loss throws a spanner in the works for the Thunder who are now placed fifth on the points table with three wins from eight games.

Brief Scores: Sydney Thunder 150/5 in 20 overs (Nadine de Klerk 36*, Tahlia Wilson 29; Linsey Smith 3-19) lost to Hobart Hurricanes 151/2 in 15.1 overs (Rachel Trenaman 55*, Lizelle Lee 42; Jemma Barsby 1-24) by 8 wickets.

Sydney Sixers registered their seventh win of the season and became the first team to qualify for the playoffs after beating the Perth Scorchers by four wickets (DLS) in Sydney on Saturday (November 21). A three-wicket haul from captain Ash Gardner helped restrict the Scorchers to 142 before a fifty from Sophia Dunkley saw the Sixers chase a revised target of 120 after the game was affected by rain.

Asked to bat first, the Scorchers started slow and were reduced to 68 for 5 by the 11th. Caoimhe Bray bowled Katie Mack before Amelia Kerr dismissed Sophie Devine and Mikayla Hinkley off successive deliveries.

There was a brief recovery through Beth Mooney and Chloe Piparo but Gardner dismissed both set batters in quick succession. She first had a well-set Mooney out stumped for 21 in the eighth over before holding on to a return catch offered by Piparo in her next over. Freya Kemp made a fighting 30-ball 43 but became Gardner’s third victim in the 18th over. The Scorchers eventually finished with 142 for 7 in 20 overs.

In pursuit, Dunkley made a blazing start, striking three sixes and four fours before play was stopped due to rain at the end of the fourth over. The chase was reduced to 16 overs, with the Sixers now chasing a revised target of 120. By then, the Sixers had already lost Ellyse Perry, and Ruby Strange struck right after the break, trapping Kerr LBW.

Dunkley and Gardner shared a brief 23-run stand before the Scorchers barged back into the contest by taking four wickets in the space of four overs while conceding just 20 runs. With the Sixers at 86 for 6, Sarah Coyte and Courtney Sippel added an unbroken 34 to finish the job in the 15th over. The loss was only the Scorchers’ second of the season and they remain well placed at second place on the points table with two games to go.

Brief Scores: Perth Scorchers 142/7 in 20 overs (Freya Kemp 43, Chloe Piparo 27; Ash Gardner 3-24) lost to Sydney Sixers 120/6 in 14.5 overs (Sophia Dunkley 54, Sarah Coyte 18*; Sophie Devine 2-22) by 4 wickets (DLS).
